verdict: Microsoft's revenue rose 18% to $82.9B as Azure grew 40% — and it poured $30.9B into new data centers in a single quarter to keep up with AI demand.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Microsoft 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics — the software businesses sell to companies; up 17% YoY. Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud grew 19% and Dynamics 365 grew 22%.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure cloud computing and server products; up 30% YoY, with Azure itself up 40%.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows, Xbox, Surface devices and search ads; down 1% YoY — Xbox content and services fell 5% and Windows OEM and Devices fell 2%, partly offset by search advertising up 12%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building new products and AI — researchers, engineers and the computing they use.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: The sales teams and advertising that sell Microsoft's products.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: The back office — finance, legal, HR and running the company.

otherDetail: Other income of $942M, net — interest and investment income, after a small $14M loss from Microsoft's stake in OpenAI.

takeaways.title: Azure is still accelerating
takeaways.text: Azure and other cloud services revenue grew 40%, Intelligent Cloud rose 30% to $34.7B, and Microsoft Cloud overall reached $54.5B — two-thirds of all revenue.

takeaways.title: The data-center bill is staggering
takeaways.text: Microsoft spent $30.9B on property and equipment in one quarter — nearly double a year ago — yet still generated $46.7B of operating cash flow and $15.8B of free cash flow.

takeaways.title: Customers have pre-committed $627B
takeaways.text: Commercial remaining performance obligation — work customers have signed for but not yet paid — jumped 99% to $627B, a backlog that underwrites future cloud revenue.

oneTimers: Losses from Microsoft's investment in OpenAI trimmed just $14M from net income this quarter — a rounding error next to the $583M drag in the same quarter a year ago.
